title: Measuring and forecasting emergent capabilities
bottleneck: Capabilities appear discontinuously with scale — sudden jumps not predicted by smaller models — yet we have no reliable science of when emergence happens or what emerges next. Scaling laws predict loss, not capabilities; evals discover jumps after the fact. This makes AI progress fundamentally unpredictable: the next training run might produce a mundane improvement or a dangerous new ability, and nobody knows which.
why_it_blocks: Governance, safety research, and business planning all assume predictable progress. Emergence makes every frontier training run a gamble.
current_state: Researchers debate whether emergence is real or a measurement artifact; forecasting remains closer to punditry than science. Labs track emergence post hoc, but no published method has reliably predicted a novel capability before training.

sources.title: An Objective Assessment of Open Problems in AI Research
